summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with HLA-B27-positive ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and obesity, was admitted for an acute worsening of chronic neck and back pain, rated as severe and limiting mobility and sleep. He presented after failing to reach his pain physician for medication refills. Initial management included IV hydromorphone and ketorolac for breakthrough pain, with continuation of home medications including OxyContin, duloxetine, and inhalers. Imaging showed no fracture but was limited by body habitus; chest X-ray revealed atelectasis without pneumonia. Inflammatory markers improved during the stay. Rheumatology and pain consultants supported symptom management without restarting biologics due to patient's prior infection concerns. Pain control improved, allowing ambulation and discharge home on unchanged narcotics. Follow-up includes continued primary care management of pain, outpatient physical therapy, and ongoing monitoring of ankylosing spondylitis.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine
